decisions.reason: As a core hardware extension of the firm’s established airfield offering with a prominent launch and likely meaningful engineering investment, management would be inclined to continue rather than admit a failed commitment.

This surveillance display fits the firm’s integrated airport-operations portfolio and had its own product presentation, so the sunk development and reputational commitment make continuation more likely than withdrawal.

Although a training program is easier to discontinue because investment is lower than for major systems, it still supports the installed base and can be justified as temporarily affected by disrupted airport activity, so management would marginally lean to keep it.

This narrowly scoped training course appears to have had the weakest public commitment and probably the lowest sunk cost, making it the easiest product for management to remove without major strategic embarrassment.

The collaboration software tool is closely aligned with the firm’s stated direction toward integrated, intelligent and collaborative airport operations, so public strategic commitment and expected future relevance favor persistence.

Because the multilateration surveillance system was presented as a flagship and focus of direction, management is especially likely to escalate commitment and keep it even if results have been slower than hoped.
